name: QuestDB
tagline: Columnar time-series SQL database built for market data and very high ingest rates.
description: QuestDB is an open-source time-series database written in low-GC Java, C++ and Rust, designed for very high ingest rates and fast time-sliced SQL. Its SQL extensions (SAMPLE BY, LATEST ON, ASOF and LT joins) make it popular with trading desks, exchanges and sensor-heavy industries. Data lands in a time-partitioned columnar format, and older partitions can be stored as Parquet. Version 10 (August 2026) added QWP, a binary columnar WebSocket protocol for both ingest and query, and live views for incrementally maintained window results. The open-source build is single-node; QuestDB Enterprise adds replication, RBAC, tiered storage and a BYOC managed option.

license.name: Apache License 2.0 (open source); Enterprise is commercial

pricing.notes: Open source is free; QuestDB Enterprise (self-managed or BYOC) is sold on contract.

scale.notes: Scales up on one large node; Enterprise replicates via object storage to read replicas and hot standbys.

strengths: Millions of rows per second ingest on a single node
Time-series SQL extensions: SAMPLE BY, LATEST ON, ASOF/LT joins, materialized and live views
Out-of-order writes are handled without a separate buffering tier
Parquet partitions keep cold data open to Spark, DuckDB and Polars
Apache-2.0 core with a strong capital-markets user base
weaknesses: No horizontal sharding; open source is a single node
Replication, RBAC and tiered storage require Enterprise
No multi-statement transactions; updates are limited compared with Postgres
useCases: Market data and order book analytics
notIdealFor: Workloads that need multi-node write scaling
